Commercial renovation in Vancouver—where Metro Vancouver's 42,000+ commercial establishments span from Kitsilano retail boutiques to Port Moody industrial warehouses, and where any renovation affecting a commercial occupancy requires coordination between the City of Vancouver's building department, Vancouver Coastal Health for food-service establishments, and Technical Safety BC for electrical and gas work—costs $50 to $400 per square foot depending on the occupancy type, scope of work, and finish level in 2026. For a typical Vancouver retail or office tenant improvement, costs range from $75 to $175 per square foot for a basic fit-out to $150 to $400 per square foot for a high-end renovation with premium finishes, mechanical upgrades, and specialized systems. Reno Stars has been completing commercial renovation projects across Vancouver, Burnaby, Richmond, and the North Shore since 2015, and Vancouver business owners should understand that commercial renovations are governed by BC Building Code Part 3 (which has substantially different requirements than the Part 9 rules applying to single-family homes), that Vancouver business licences must be updated when a tenant improvement changes the nature of the business, and that the Vancouver Fire Code imposes specific requirements on commercial occupancies that do not apply to residential renovations.

Vancouver Commercial Renovation Permits and Requirements

Commercial renovation in Vancouver requires navigating multiple regulatory frameworks that do not apply to residential work:

  • BC Building Code Part 3 governs commercial occupancies in Vancouver, setting substantially higher requirements than the Part 9 rules for single-family homes. Part 3 covers fire alarm systems, emergency lighting, accessibility requirements (BC Building Code Section 3.8), fire separations, occupancy classifications, and exiting requirements. Every commercial renovation in Vancouver must comply with the occupancy classification assigned at the time of the building's original permit.
  • The City of Vancouver's building permit is required for all commercial tenant improvements, change of use, and substantial renovations. Vancouver Commercial building permits require drawings prepared by a registered professional (architect or engineer) for any work affecting structural elements, fire-rated assemblies, or accessibility features. Permit processing time at the City of Vancouver for commercial projects is typically 4–8 weeks, longer than residential due to the additional review complexity.
  • Vancouver Coastal Health approval is required for any commercial renovation involving food service, including restaurants, cafes, bakeries, food courts, and any business where food is prepared, stored, or served to the public. This includes new food establishment permits, significant renovations to existing food establishments, and any change of use to a food-service occupancy. Vancouver Coastal Health reviews floor plans, equipment specifications, ventilation systems, and sanitation facilities.
  • Technical Safety BC permits are required for all gas and electrical work in Vancouver commercial occupancies, including gas cooking equipment, gas-fired HVAC, commercial kitchen suppression systems, and electrical service upgrades. All gas work must be performed by a registered gas contractor with a Vancouver-area permit.
  • The Vancouver Fire Code applies to all commercial occupancies and is enforced by the Vancouver Fire Department. The Fire Code imposes requirements for fire alarm system maintenance, exiting path clearance, fire extinguisher placement, and fire suppression system maintenance that must be maintained during and after any renovation. Any work affecting a fire suppression system (sprinklers, standpipes) requires a Vancouver fire permit.
  • Accessibility requirements under BC Building Code Section 3.8 apply to all commercial renovations in Vancouver. This includes minimum doorway widths, accessible washroom requirements, ramp specifications, and tactile indicators. Vancouver's own bylaws may impose additional accessibility requirements beyond the BC Building Code minimums.
  • The Commercial Tenancy Act (BC) governs the relationship between Vancouver commercial landlords and tenants. Tenant improvements in Vancouver typically require landlord approval, and the tenancy agreement typically specifies who is responsible for the cost of improvements, whether improvements become the landlord's property at lease end, and what condition the premises must be returned to at lease end.
  • Vancouver business licences must be updated when a tenant improvement changes the nature or scope of the business being conducted at the premises. A change from retail to restaurant use, for example, requires both a new Vancouver business licence and a new Vancouver Coastal Health food establishment permit.

Frequently Asked Questions About Commercial Renovation in Vancouver

What permits do I need for a commercial renovation in Vancouver?

The permits required for a commercial renovation in Vancouver depend on the scope of work and the occupancy type. A Vancouver building permit is always required for commercial tenant improvements, change of use, and any work affecting structural elements, fire-rated assemblies, accessibility features, or building systems. All commercial building permit applications in Vancouver require drawings prepared by a registered professional (architect or registered professional engineer) for any work affecting fire safety, structural, mechanical, or accessibility elements. Additionally, Vancouver Coastal Health approval is required for any food-service establishment, Technical Safety BC gas and electrical permits are required for all gas and electrical work, and the Vancouver Fire Department may require a permit for work affecting fire suppression systems. The City of Vancouver business licence must also be updated if the renovation changes the nature of the business. Processing times for commercial building permits at the City of Vancouver are typically 4–8 weeks due to the additional review complexity compared to residential permits. Reno Stars manages the complete Vancouver commercial renovation permit process for our clients, including coordinating with architects, engineers, Vancouver Coastal Health, and Technical Safety BC.

How much does a Vancouver restaurant renovation cost in 2026?

A Vancouver restaurant renovation costs $150 to $700 per square foot in 2026 depending on the restaurant type and finish level. A fast-casual Vancouver restaurant renovation (counter service, minimal kitchen equipment) typically costs $150 to $250 per square foot. A full-service Vancouver restaurant renovation (table service, full commercial kitchen) typically costs $250 to $400 per square foot. A high-end Vancouver fine dining restaurant renovation with premium finishes, specialized kitchen equipment, and complex HVAC requirements can cost $400 to $700 per square foot. These costs include general construction, mechanical and electrical work, and Vancouver permit fees, but do not include the cost of kitchen equipment (which can add $50,000 to $500,000 depending on the scope), architectural and engineering fees (8–15% of construction cost in Vancouver), or Vancouver Coastal Health food establishment permit fees. A 1,500 square foot full-service Vancouver restaurant renovation would typically total $375,000 to $600,000 excluding kitchen equipment. Vancouver restaurant renovations also require Vancouver Coastal Health approval of the kitchen design, Technical Safety BC gas permits for cooking equipment, and Vancouver Fire Department review of fire suppression systems.

Does the Commercial Tenancy Act affect my Vancouver renovation?

Yes—the BC Commercial Tenancy Act directly affects how Vancouver commercial renovations are planned, funded, and managed. Under the Commercial Tenancy Act, tenant improvements in Vancouver typically require written landlord approval before any work begins, and the tenancy agreement specifies who bears the cost of improvements, whether improvements become the landlord's property at lease end, and what condition the premises must be returned to at lease end (often "base building condition" which may require the tenant to remove their improvements). Vancouver commercial tenants should negotiate a tenant improvement allowance (TIA) as part of their lease—a landlord contribution to the cost of the initial fit-out that does not require repayment. TIAs in Vancouver typically range from $10 to $75 per square foot depending on the location, building class, and lease term. Tenants should also negotiate that their improvements become the landlord's property at lease end (rather than requiring removal and restoration) or negotiate a depreciation schedule that allows the tenant to amortize improvement costs over the lease term. Any Vancouver commercial renovation should be reviewed by a commercial tenancy lawyer before the lease is signed, not after a dispute arises.
